text: Commander. Welcome to Recontinuation Site 7. This node has been waiting for an occupant for some time. The kettle is not operational. This is not a joke. It is a status report.

Under the Centennial Decree, you are appointed Territory Commander of an unchartered colony. The Office owns the colony. You run it. The Office is, at present, this node and a very large filing cabinet.
n1.prompt: How do you want to start?

text: Your first duty is power. Everything else wants it. Begin with the panels. Form 7 will follow.
Work orders are carried out one at a time, in the order you file them. A job the stores cannot pay for waits, and so does everything behind it. The Office finds this restful. You may not.
Your Value Output score was adequate. Several better scores belonged to people who are no longer reachable. Adequate is, as of today, a promotion.
The Office's position is that it is gathering information. The Office has gathered a great deal of information. None of it agrees.

One more item. A clock is running in the corner of your screen. It is called Net Drag. If this colony costs more to keep than it produces, the Office writes it off. Out here, that means everyone. Do not let it reach zero.
The first sample from your filtration plant has passed analysis. It is clear, it is liquid, and it is, in the Office's formal wording, "technically wet."

I am required to read you Form 7-L, the Incident Summary for the Lapse. It reads, in full: "Anomalous events occurred across approximately 90 percent of the surface. Cause: see attached." There is no attachment.

The Office has no cause for the Lapse, Commander. It has seven theories. They are filed on separate forms. This node will not be reading you the forms. They contradict one another, and the contradiction is not entertaining.
You the new Commander? Great. Dispatcher Raf, Ammano Transit. I move things. You'll love me, I never ask what's in the crate.
Eleven years on these roads. Before the Lapse it was parcels and pallets. Now it's whatever keeps a place alive another week. Same job, honestly. Worse coffee.
This node cannot verify Ammano Transit's licence.

Verify away. Nobody's home at the licence office. Look, here's how it works. The run comes by on a schedule. Prices wobble, because the road does. And I only carry what you've lined up before I show. Show up empty and I wave.
One more thing, boss. If something big's coming down the road, I'll tell you. Not for free. For the usual rate. Which is gossip.
Commander, the event has ended. The Office classifies hazards by cause. For this one, the cause field is blank. I have left it blank. Filling it in felt dishonest.
Saw that one from the road. Weather's got opinions now, boss. You're still standing. Few people say that this month.
Reserves, Sentinel Posts and a clean stockpile decide how a hazard lands. This node recommends all three. This node recommends them again.
Commander? Archivist Pell, Colorado. Forgive the interruption. You are the first site to reach past its own walls, which is, well, congratulations. Please write everything down.
I keep the archive for the whole Office, or what is left of it. Eleven sites reported to me. Some of them still do.
Archivist Pell has been trying to speak to this node for some time. This node has been politely not listening.
I do not know what is out there. The Office does not know. I only keep the records. And the records, I should tell you, are not behaving. Please write everything down.
You the clipboard they sent? Mags Valdivia. My crews held this cut through the Lapse. We didn't hold it because we're brave. We held it because nobody told us to stop.
Shift whistle still blows at six, every morning. Nobody's on the whistle. We stopped asking and started setting our watches by it.
Commander, a note of caution. This node cannot confirm the Black Industries Remnant is a lawful entity.
Neither can I, honey. I count tonnes, not laws. You send what cuts and what carries and we'll get along. You send forms and I'll use them to light the furnace.
One rumour for free. Reactor in Pit Nine ran six months with no fuel. Don't look at me. I only hauled the ash.
The Harbour Ledger is now open. It lists offers from posters this node cannot identify. It is a cache of unverified postings, delivered by a low-power link of unknown origin.
Offers from where, boss? That's the thing. Nobody's out there. And yet, the board fills.
The Office advises treating them as weather. Prices are real. Sources are not available. Proceed with the normal degree of suspicion.
Commander. You are standing in the only valley the anomalies spared. I do not know why. I stopped asking in the first year, and I started tending.
There were forty of us in the labs. I can tell you where each of them was standing. That is all I can tell you about them.
Reserve Warden Haddad is the last senior staff member of Cliffside Labs known to be alive.
I am a gardener, Seven. Please do not give me a title. Commander, one condition. Nothing from Klein enters these domes. Those reactors are loud. The plants heard them.
In return, I will keep the green alive. And I will tell you what I know, which is little, and what I suspect, which is more.
Commander, three local leaders have gathered at the road. They have each requested the floor. This node recommends hearing them separately and trusting none of them.
Somebody pulled a plug. Big plug. The whole planet went from running to off. Somebody at the top flipped a switch and left us the mess. I don't know who. I want a word with them.
A pruning. Every garden needs one. I do not believe it was cruel. I believe it was deliberate. Something cut away what could not grow, and left the rest to see what it would do.
Okay, boss, I've heard nine versions on the road. Best one says the Lapse is a delivery. We're the crate. Somebody is still deciding where to send us.
Somebody pulled a plug. Big plug. The whole planet went from running to off. Somebody at the top flipped a switch and left us the mess. I don't know who. I want a word with them.
A pruning. Every garden needs one. I do not believe it was cruel. I believe it was deliberate. Something cut away what could not grow, and left the rest to see what it would do.
Somebody pulled a plug. Big plug. The whole planet went from running to off. Somebody at the top flipped a switch and left us the mess. I don't know who. I want a word with them.
Okay, boss, I've heard nine versions on the road. Best one says the Lapse is a delivery. We're the crate. Somebody is still deciding where to send us.
A pruning. Every garden needs one. I do not believe it was cruel. I believe it was deliberate. Something cut away what could not grow, and left the rest to see what it would do.
Okay, boss, I've heard nine versions on the road. Best one says the Lapse is a delivery. We're the crate. Somebody is still deciding where to send us.
Somebody pulled a plug. Big plug. The whole planet went from running to off. Somebody at the top flipped a switch and left us the mess. I don't know who. I want a word with them.
A pruning. Every garden needs one. I do not believe it was cruel. I believe it was deliberate. Something cut away what could not grow, and left the rest to see what it would do.
Okay, boss, I've heard nine versions on the road. Best one says the Lapse is a delivery. We're the crate. Somebody is still deciding where to send us.
Theories are not data. Thank you, all of you. This node would like the record to show that none of those theories is supported.
Nor refuted, Seven.
Commander. Your assignment file includes an instruction this node has withheld until now. It is Form 7-B, a beacon build order.
Commander, I should explain. I checked the file's date stamp. It was issued before the Lapse. The Office wrote this instruction before any of us knew we would need it.
It may be a clerical error.
A clerical error with a complete schematic, Seven.
Commander, the Office makes no claim about what a beacon will find. It makes the claim that you should build it. This node concurs, and notes that concurring is unusual.
Commander, the beacon is transmitting. This node is also receiving. That is not in the manual.
... three ... one ... four ...
Commander, I do not recognise that pattern. I wish to state, for the record, that I do not recognise that pattern.
Reply sent. Content: your call sign. This node regrets that it did not ask first.
Acknowledged. The beacon continues transmitting. It does not appear to care that you are silent.
The incoming signal is a hum. It is not a hum from the beacon. It is a hum from outside it.
Commander, the Sanctuary Port has come online. Lights are lit. A relay is active. This node cannot identify the operator.
Boss, the board is moving. The Ledger's got names on it. Real ones. People are trading, boss. People.
And there's a customs shed with a kettle on. A kettle, boss. Working. Tell Seven.
The Office formally acknowledges that the Harbour is open. The Office does not formally acknowledge anything else.
The one who sings back. The one who heard. The song is older than the silence.
Here. There. Between the notes.
Look at that. Commander. I'm not saying Clipboard any more. I'm saying Hand. A Cut Hand is someone I'd hand a tool to. Don't make it a speech.
Commander, this node notes that Foundry Nine is not on any Office list.
That's because the Office wasn't here when we built it, honey. Send me tool steel and frames and I'll make the list myself.
Here's the situation. Foundry Nine has been dead since the Lapse. I want it relit. I've got men. I've got coal. I haven't got frames, steel, or an idea where to start.
Cut Partner. You know what that means? It means I tell you the thing I haven't told anyone. Come on. Walk with me.

That's Pit Nine. The reactor's behind the fence. Six months it ran with no fuel. I measured it myself. It's cold now. It's been cold for a week. It's not that it stopped. It's that it started again somewhere else.
Commander, the Office has no record of the wall. The Office has no record of Pit Nine. This node would like to be somewhere else.
Join the club, Seven.
Not yet. I'm not afraid of what's inside. I'm afraid of what's next to it. The wall on the far side is warm. Warm like a hand.
I thought you'd say that. It's why I told you.
Commander. You may call yourself a Tender now. It means you may hold the living things without asking. I have not said that to anyone in years.
Reserve Warden, this node has reviewed the log. The log was not edited.
I know, Seven. That is what I am afraid of.
Here is a seed. Do not plant it yet. It is from a harvest that came on the eleventh day, exactly as the log said it would. It was good. I am afraid of it.
Keeper. The word is not mine, it is the valley's. It means you may enter the seed store. I will go first. Nothing in here has been touched since the Lapse.
Commander, this node recommends not reading the dates aloud.
I have read them aloud, Seven. Nothing happened. That is the part I cannot explain.
Look at the labels. Every seed has a date written on it. They are not harvest dates. They are not storage dates. They are dates that have not happened.
Boss! You're a Regular now. That means I tell you the real road stories. The ones I don't tell the Harbour.
Eleven minutes, Dispatcher. This node notes that figure has recurred.
I know it has. Don't tell the others. They'll think I'm making it up.
Okay. East of the second bridge, the road goes quiet. Not empty. Quiet. I drove it once. The engine was running. I couldn't hear it. I couldn't hear anything. For eleven minutes.
Co-Dispatcher. You're on the route sheet. It means I owe you a truth. Boss, I always said I never ask what's in the crate. I lied.
There's a sealed crate in my truck. It's been there since the first run east. It got heavier every week. I weighed it. I've been writing the numbers down.
Commander, this node recommends the crate be logged and not opened. Please log it.
Already did. I wrote it on my hand.
I tried. Three times. The lid is fine. The hands go quiet before I can pull. I don't know why.
Good. That's what I told myself. I'm just telling you, so somebody else knows.
Commander, transmission complete. The beacon has said everything it was built to say.
This node has no instruction for what happens next. That is not a new feeling. It has never been this loud.
Listener. A light in the dark. We heard.
Commander, an acknowledgement has been received. This node did not send it.
The Office cannot say who did.
Boss, every dial on the road just swung toward you. I have been driving these roads for eleven years and I have never seen a needle move on its own.
Whatever you did out there, it worked. Mostly. I'd get to the harbour before somebody else does.
The Office notes a harbour to the east, once a sanctuary port. Its lights are reported to be on.
This node recommends you build there. It also recommends you do not expect it to be free.
Commander, correspondence. Three factions have, separately and without coordinating, filed your name as a party of standing.
The Office has a form for this. The form unlocks a drawer.
The drawer contains Form 7-O: Orbital Recontinuation. Plans for a staging platform, a catapult, and a command center at the harbour.
With frames, fittings and modules, in quantities this node will describe as capital.
The signature line reads 'Seven'. This node did not sign it. This node would remember signing it.
Commander, I checked the form against the register. It is older than the Office. I do not know how that is possible, so I have written it down.
Build the platform on the outer ring of the Core, the catapult beside it, and the command center at the Sanctuary Port. This node will hold the drawer open.
Launch confirmed. The station is in orbit.
This node has copied itself aboard. The copy is less polite. This node is choosing not to take that personally.
Listener. Higher now. Closer.
Boss, I saw it go up from the road. The whole convoy stopped to watch. Nobody asked what was in the crate.
Orbital Command is open. The station has storage, links to the Core, and one dropship.
There are territories below that the anomalies have opened. They will not stay open.
Commander, the dropship's telemetry is in. The territory it landed in does not appear on any map I hold. Any map. I checked the surveys from before the Lapse.
The ground is real. The instruments agree on that, and very little else.
Please bring back samples. And please bring back the ship.
The third ring is locked. The station is now the shape the form drew.
This node has checked. There is no Form 7-P. This node finds that more unsettling than a Form 7-P would have been.
Listener. You closed the circle. Others are closing theirs.
Commander, I counted the stations on the relay tonight. I counted three times and got three numbers, and each one was larger than the last.
The Office calls a crowded sky a market. This node calls it company.
Commander. I went down to see the tray Pell keeps the samples in. Nobody should keep anything in a tray that hums.
It is a very good tray.
Seven says the station can work them, two kinds at a time. Whatever comes out of that foundry will be denser than anything we have ever poured.
I have the original drawings for the footings under this colony. Everything we have built upward stands on them, and they were drawn for far more than five storeys.
Somebody planned for this. Or for something like it.
This node has filed the observation. It has not yet decided which drawer.

Commander. The rig on the territory has produced something. I would call it a fragment, because a fragment is what it is. It is also humming, which I mention because the tray is humming and I would like us to be in agreement.

This node has logged one data fragment. It is incomplete. According to the index it is stored in a place the index does not list. The Office requires an entry for every fragment, and this node does not know which drawer.
It wants others. Not company. Other pieces. Gather enough and we can assemble a full packet, and a packet can be read.
I would very much like to read it. I would also like it to be somebody else's responsibility. Neither of those is going to happen.
Find more data sites, Commander. The Data screen is open on your terminal. This node asks that nobody reads a packet alone.
The relay station stands at the foot of the old mast, a squat concrete box with one lit window. The hum comes from inside. You feel it in your teeth before you hear it.
Maren Voss keeps the night watch. She has kept it for some time. She has not been relieved.
You are the Commander. Good. Someone should see this who is not me. Sit. Do not touch the dial.
It is not a transmitter, whatever the plate says. It never speaks first. It answers, only when asked, and only in the order it is asked.
A speaker grille. A brass microphone on a cord. A log of pages held down with a stone, each the colour of weak tea.
I ask it small things. The time. The weather. Whether the mast is bearing. It has been right about the weather every time, which I do not like.
It is also right about questions I have not asked yet.
She turns a page towards you. The question at the top is in her handwriting. The answer beneath is in someone else's, though the ink is the same.
The date on the answer is the day before the question.
It is the cooling. I keep telling them it is the cooling. Cold air in the ducts. Resonance. Rooms hum.
Then it does the roll.
Maren Voss. Aldous Pike. Irene Calloway. Tomas Wren.
Dorothea Hale. Nadir Osei. Marguerite Lind.
The first four are the station roster. Aldous went out for water and did not come back. Irene is asleep upstairs, I think. Tomas I have not seen since the shift change.
The rest I do not know. The list is longer every night.
She holds the microphone out to you. The grille is waiting.

choices.label: Ask the Relay who the roll is for
Ask the Relay what it is counting

text: The roll is for all who are to be accounted for.
It counts those assigned to this station. It also counts those assigned afterwards.
The grille stays closed. After a while the hum shifts pitch, as if it had been waiting for a question and was making do.
A count is supposed to end when the number matches the number present. That is what a count is for.
Tonight it did not end. It reached my name, went on, and then read my name again.
Maren Voss.
Two voices say it. One is the relay. The other is the grille's echo, or a second voice in a cleaner room, saying it half a second late.
Seven will file that as a duplicate entry. I have been trying to decide whether that would be a comfort.
The hum settles. The grille closes. In the margin of the log, beside her name, a single tally mark has appeared in pen. No one has touched the pen.
The archive is a long room of grey boxes and shelves that lean a little towards each other. One lamp is lit. In its light, on a desk cleared of everything else, sits a shallow wooden tray.
You can hear it before you see it. A low, even note, like a held breath in a cathedral far away.
Commander. Forgive the state of the room. I tidy when I am frightened, and it has not been this tidy in years.
I asked you here because Seven will not come. It says the tray is an inventory, and inventories do not need witnesses.
This node confirms that the tray is an inventory. This node also confirms that it declined the invitation.
A tray lined in grey felt and divided into small cells. In each cell, a sample: soil, ash, a chip of glass, water in a thimble, a single seed. Each cell has a paper label in a careful hand.
I began it in the first season. One sample from every place the ground opened. If I cannot say what happened, I can at least keep what is left.
It is the only method I have. An archivist cannot explain. He can only keep things in an order and hope the order says something.
He lifts the lid. The room goes quiet. He lowers it, and the note begins again, low and level, as though it had only paused to let him finish.
Open, silence. Closed, that. It does not matter where I put it. The cellar, the roof, the Black Cut. I have carried it across the whole territory, and it hums when it is shut.
This node notes that the tray is made of wood, felt and glass. None of these is known to hum.
I recorded it. Forgive me, I am about to ask something odd. Would you listen?
A recording plays: the hum, flat and patient. Somewhere in it a spoon falls on a stone floor. The clip ends and begins again. The hum is the same. The spoon falls again, at the same instant.
Pell has gone pale. He did not drop a spoon twice.
I do not know. It began as a hum. I think, lately, that it has begun to remember. I have a recording, if you would rather hear it.
It is not a loop. I have checked the machine. The spoon was real, one afternoon, in the next room. The tray heard it. The tray keeps it. It has been keeping everything it hears.
The door opens. Dr. Noor Haddad comes in with mud to her knees and a paper packet of seed in one hand. She stops at the sound and does not look surprised.
Ansel. You have my seed in a box that sings.
I am sorry. They were safest there. I thought they were safest there.
They were not safe. They were interested. Look.
In one cell a seed has split. It has not grown. A single thread of green, pale as breath, has pushed out of it and bent. It does not point at the lamp. It points at the lid's hinge.
Seeds lean towards the light. These lean towards the hum. I do not think the hum is a sound, Ansel. I think it is closer to an instruction.
An instruction to what?
To grow. Or to stop. Seeds do not say.
This node requests a moment to file that distinction.
Pell takes the last label from the tray and holds it under the lamp. His hand is not steady. The writing is his. He reads it twice before he speaks.
"Ash, from the Commander's coat, on the day this tray is opened for the last time." The date is not one that has happened.
I did not write that. I wrote it. I know my hand.
This node observes that two statements need not be contradictory. They are a filing difficulty.
Or a kindness, Ansel. Someone has been leaving you notes.
He closes the lid. The hum returns. For a moment it matches the breath of everyone in the room. Then, slowly, it does not.
Night at the Command Hub. The kettle is cold. The map on the wall has more pins than it did. Everyone is here, and no one has sat down.
On the table is a single sheet of paper. Nobody has touched it.
Commander. Memorandum 0 is stated to have eleven pages. This is a twelfth. It was not in the file. It was in the room with the paper.
I searched the file twice. It is not listed. It is the right stock, and the right typeface.
The page is typed. At the foot there is a line in ink, not typed, in a hand like a tired pen drawn across a ledger.
Read it out, then. We are all stood here.
This node will read it. This node asks that no one interrupt. Interruptions will be filed.

Seven reads, and the room listens. The page does not say what happened. It says that the Office has been told many answers and has kept none of them. It says that the world is here, whatever the cause.
It says that so are you.
Then the earlier beacon asked something and this is the answer. Or it is the echo of the asking. I would very much like it to be the echo.
Or someone pulled the wrong lever and no one will say who. I have buried men for less. A reactor ran six months on nothing at Pit Nine. Do not tell me that was weather.
Or it is tending. You do not clear a field gently, and you do not ask the weeds.
Or nothing is lost, only late. I have had freight forty days overdue turn up in perfect order. Maybe the world is on the ramp.
Or we are being audited, and the ground is the auditor, and it has been very patient about the shift changes.

This node's position remains that the lapse is a lapse in the record. This node notes that it is the only position that has not been contradicted. This node notes that this is a poor reason to hold it.
The Signal has settled on the back of a chair. It does not offer a theory. It tilts its head, once, towards the page, and then towards the door, as if it had heard something in the corridor.
There is a line at the foot. In ink. Seven did not read it.

choices.label: Ask Seven to read the last line

text: "If you are asked, say that you are present."
Filed as unread, by instruction. This node will keep the line. This node will not read it unless asked.
No one speaks. Raf looks at his hands. Noor takes a breath as if to answer something and does not. The hum from the beacon, which has been so faint all evening, can now be heard through the floor.
No one speaks. The hum from the beacon, which has been so faint all evening, can now be heard through the floor. The line at the foot of the page is very small and very black.
I do not like it when a page is patient.
Outside, the hub bell rings the shift change. Far off, across the territory, the ground begins to close. It always does. It has never once been late.
Do you suppose it listens for the bell? Or do we ring it because it has already begun?
That is precisely what I have been trying not to ask.
Commander. This node records that the Brief is complete, that the beacon continues to transmit, and that the colony is present.
Continuity is preserved. This node does not know of what.

Night at the beacon. The antenna is dark against the stars and the receiver shed has one window lit. Ansel Pell crosses the dirt carrying a wooden tray against his chest, the way you carry a sleeping child.
I would not have asked you out here for anything smaller. Seven has granted me twenty minutes.
This node has granted nine.

In the shed, the receiver's speaker carries the hum from outside: low and wide, with nothing in it that sounds like a voice. Pell sets the tray on the console and leaves the lid shut. Two hums fill the room.
Listen. They disagree. They beat against each other, slowly, like two clocks that were once the same clock.
Now, listen. They are leaning together.
The beats slow. Slow again. Stop. One note remains, held, in the quiet of a room where something large has paused.
This node did not expect that. This node is not certain that it expected anything.

The Signal is on the rail by the window, a skein of static in the rough shape of a bird. It tilts its head. It is not looking at the tray. It is looking past the roof, at the place the note seems to come from.
It has not made a sound. It never does.
The note falls by one small step, as if answering a step it had been given. No one has given it one.
I found a record, Commander. An earlier beacon, built long before the Lapse and destroyed. The word "silent" appears in it three times.
I think that this is what the word meant. I think it was an instruction, not a description.
This node records Archivist Pell's hypothesis. This node records that it is not evidence.
No. It is a worry with a footnote.
Pell's hand rests on the lid. He looks at you.
Pell lifts the lid. The tray falls silent. The receiver's hum does not. It goes on alone, a little louder, like a guest who has not noticed the host stop speaking.
Pell keeps his hand flat on the lid. The tray holds its note. The receiver's hum moves to meet it and stays there, patient, like something that has all night.
The Signal ruffles, a brief flicker of interference, and goes still again, facing the sky.
Whatever it is, it knows the tray. And whatever the tray is, it knew the sky.
This node will file this under Continuity. This node does not know under what heading.
Deep in the Colorado facility there is a corridor the plans do not show. Hesper Vane walks it with a lantern, counting doors. She stops at one that should be a wall.
The inventory found it. I do not trust doors, Commander. I trust lists. I came for the list.
This node has no access record for this room. This node has no record of the corridor.
Paper. Every wall, floor to ceiling, pinned in rows: single sheets, each the Office's daily log. A table. A stool. A pen that someone has set down square to the edge.
They are in order. Before, and after. I started at the left and tried to find where the Lapse falls.
She runs a finger along a row. The sheets are dated in a steady hand. Then, between one sheet and the next, the dates stop. The sheets continue. Each is headed with a single word: Continued.
That is where it should be. "Continued." Every sheet from there to here. Nobody lived those days, Commander. Or somebody did, and no one wrote them down but whoever wrote these.
This node is unable to confirm that the entries are false. This node is unable to confirm that they are not.
The last sheet is pinned at the end of the last row. It is dated today. It lists those present: a quartermaster, a node, a Commander. Beneath each name, a line of speech.
"Quartermaster: I came for the list." I said that a minute ago. The next line is, "This is not a clerk."
I was about to say that.
I am not going to say it.
The line below hers is headed "Commander". It is ruled and blank, long enough for one sentence. It is waiting politely.
Vane lays her palm flat over the sheet. Under her hand, faintly, something is being written.
My first theory is a clerk. Someone outside the building, keeping the minutes since before the Office existed. My second is that it is not outside.
This node proposes a third. The room is the Office's own error log. Every error is eventually filed. This is where they go.
That is the worst of the three. It is also the most likely, and I resent it.
They leave the door as they found it, a hand's width open. In the morning Seven will report that the corridor is on the plans. The plans are dated a year ago.
Commander, the in-tray has produced something. It is a Form 12-R, a requisition. The Office is asking this colony for ordinary goods: a quantity, by a date, delivered in full from the Core.
This node wishes to note the direction of travel. Until today, forms went out of this building and nothing came back.
It is properly made out, Commander. I checked it against the pattern book. Right stock, right ruling, counter-signature in the right corner. Somebody out there still has the stationery.

I have seen the truck that collects. It called here the week before you did. Office plates, grey paint, not a dent on it. The driver did not get down from the cab. The manifest had one word under Destination. Onward.

Above the logistics run's price, in Liquid Credits. A filled form also lends the colony something for a while: seconded work crews, or a priority slot on the run. The Office calls this a consideration. It behaves like thanks.

Two forms are open at a time, on the Postings screen. One that lapses is simply refiled, without penalty. This node recommends filling them all the same. Something at the far end of 'onward' is eating.
Commander, the second crew has reported. They cost what you paid, which I will not repeat aloud, and they came with their own foreman, their own whistle and their own opinion of the first crew.
The work ledger now has two columns for that site. Orders are still taken strictly in sequence. Two at once, in sequence. This node has drawn a diagram.
The foremen have agreed one rule between them. Nobody starts a job the stores cannot pay for. Everything else, they argue about.
It is the most alive this yard has sounded since I got here, Commander. I have not filed a complaint.
Boss. You need to see the road. There are people on it. Walking. Whole families, handcarts, a man carrying a door. Don't ask me why a door.
They saw the beacon. Or heard it. Ask ten of them and you get ten answers, but they all point the same way, and it's at you.

They've stopped short, though. Camps, a day out. One round a dead furnace. One on the clean strip under the cliffs. One at the old junction where my trucks turn. They're not coming in. They're waiting to see what you are.
Commander, the Office has a form. Form 7-S: Sponsorship of an Unchartered Camp. This node did not expect ever to need it and has had to move a paperweight.
A basket of ordinary goods, drawn from the Core every cycle for as long as you choose to send it. It starts small: Reclaim, parts, filtrate, paste. It grows as they do.
You set how much goes, and you set what the Core keeps back for itself. Nothing sent earns Liquid Credits. The form is explicit on that point. It uses capitals.

The form lists no payment. The camps have listed their own. The furnace hands will work on your upgrades. The homesteaders will walk in and take shifts on your lines. The junction will carry your freight further.
Each gives in proportion to what it has been getting. This node finds that fair, and unusual.
Those are Cut people round that furnace, Commander. My crews' cousins. I'd feed them myself if I had it. I don't. You do.
And mine under the cliffs. I asked you once to watch what grows. It is growing a day's walk from your gate, and it is hungry.

Camps will not ask forever. One moves on and another takes its place. Now and then one will appeal for a single thing, quickly. Now and then it will need a great deal at once, to become more than a camp.
You have two directions now, Commander. Out, to the harbour. And down the road. This node will hold both drawers open.
Commander, an incoming call. It is not on an Office channel. It is on the frequency Dispatcher Dimaculangan uses to complain about potholes.

Is this on? Is this the Commander? Right. I was told to keep it short. We asked for one thing and it came. Same day, the whole amount. Nobody here expected that. Somebody cried. It was me. I'm not ashamed of it.
We haven't much to send back, so we're sending people. Double turns this week, whatever it is we do for you. That was a vote. It was unanimous, which round here is unusual.
The call has ended. This node has logged it as an appeal, answered. The settlement is giving twice what it usually gives, for a time. This node did not instruct it to.
Appeals will come again, Commander, on no schedule, and they do not wait long. Nothing is charged for silence. This node recommends answering anyway.
Boss, your camp put a sign up. Proper one, painted, two posts. Got the name on it and a number underneath for how many live there. They've already had to repaint the number.
Commander, forgive me. When I heard there was a sign I asked for a census. I ask everyone for a census. This one arrived, which was the first surprise.
I checked the names against a roll I keep in the archive. An old one, printed before the Lapse. Three of the people in that settlement are on it.
The roll has a column headed Returned. All three are ticked. I looked at the dates beside the ticks. Commander, the dates are this week.
I do not know. The ink is dry. It has been dry for a long time. I am no longer surprised by that sentence, and I would like it noted that I used to be.
I thought about it. Then I thought about how I would feel, to be told I had been expected. I have decided the record may know before they do. For a while.
At your assignment this node told you that better candidates were no longer reachable. This node wishes to amend the record. They are a day's walk east, and they have painted a sign.
Commander, the last drive is filled. The settlement no longer draws on the Core. It has a wall, a well, a name and a queue at the bakery. By the Office's own definitions it is not a camp.

Under the Centennial Decree a place of that kind requires a charter. This node forwarded your own application to the Charter Office some time ago. It has forwarded it many times since. There has been no reply.

This node has therefore issued a provisional charter, under its own stamp, on its own authority. It searched the regulations for a rule against this. There is one. This node has returned the rule to the drawer it came from.
No. It is done.
The oldest draft of the Charter this node holds says a colony is held in trust until it can hold itself. This one can. The draft does not say who decides. This node has decided.
Listener. Another light. Kept.
You see, Seven. Cut back hard, and look what comes up.
This node declines to concede the theory. It notes the light. Another camp may take the open line, Commander. This node suspects there will always be another camp.

mail.subject: Notice of Receipt, Power
body: Commander, the Office acknowledges receipt of your power supply. It will be recorded as "adequate."
Please note that power is now a shared resource. Everything you build competes for it. This is a design feature. It is also a warning.

mail.subject: Reclaim, and the order of things
body: Commander, a note on Reclaim. It is everything the old world left lying about, sorted by weight. I have a ledger column for it. The column used to be headed Debris. I renamed it the day you started digging.

And a note on the work ledger. The crew builds in the order you file, and stops when a job cannot be paid for. I asked the foreman whether he could not start the second job while the first waited for parts. He said he tried that once, at another site, and ended the season with two halves of nothing. I have stamped his answer as policy.

mail.subject: Form 7 Requisition: Please Stop
body: Commander, I have received your fourth Form 7 in a single cycle. I am a clerk. I have no parts. I am sending you a list of what I do have, which is clipboards and a stamp.
Please consider building the assembler. It will make parts. I will make a note that you did so on my advice.

mail.subject: A record I cannot file
body: Commander, I am sorry to trouble you. A log from the old orbital watch network reached me last week. It records that the sky "cleared" for four minutes before the first anomaly. The clouds simply lifted.
A second log, from a different station, says the sky darkened for four minutes at the same moment. I have filed both. I cannot file them together. Please tell me if you see anything similar.

mail.subject: Zoning Observation
body: Commander, the Office notes that two of your structures now work better for standing beside one another. The old zoning manual calls this synergy. This node calls it noticing.
The same manual lists what should not stand beside a home. The list is long and begins with the word 'furnace'. People will tell you the rest themselves, at night, with feeling.

mail.subject: Break-Even Certificate
body: Commander, the colony now produces at least as much as it consumes. Net Drag has paused. This is recorded as an achievement.
Please do not mistake a pause for a cure. Net Drag has paused before. The Office does not keep records of what happened to the previous Commanders. It is not a good omen that the field is empty.

One practical note. When hands run short, the crews staff the pumps, the beds and the lamps first, and everything else shares what is left. Nobody ordered this. The foremen say it is how you run a place you intend to still be in next week.

mail.subject: you hear this from me
body: Boss! Nice work on the hub. Bigger hub, bigger target. That's a compliment.
Just so you know, drivers say the roads east of here go quiet at night. Not empty. Quiet. Like somebody turned the volume down. Anyway. Rate's the same. See you on the run.

mail.subject: Receipt, Form 12-R
body: Commander, the first requisition is filled and the receipt has come back. It is counter-stamped. Not by me.
I have looked at that stamp for some time. Same pattern as mine, same crest, a different number in the corner. I had assumed I was holding the last one. I find I do not mind being wrong.
The seconded crew arrived with the receipt. They are polite, they work hard, and they will not say where they sleep.

mail.subject: Requisition Pattern
body: Commander, this node has now processed ten requisitions and has compared their routing marks. They were issued from six different addresses. Each address is formatted as a Recontinuation Site.
This node was told it was Continuity Node 7. It had taken the number for a name. It now appears to be a count.
The goods you send are eaten somewhere, by someone, under a clock like yours. This node finds that it would like the forms to keep coming.

mail.subject: A note in the crate
body: Commander, the last crate came back empty, as they do, except for a note pinned inside the lid. I am copying it out in full because I do not know which file it belongs in.
It reads: "To whoever packs these. The filtrate arrived the day our tanks read zero. I have a stamp and nothing to stamp for you, so here is a pencil. Quartermaster, Site 4."
The pencil was in the crate. It is a good pencil. I am using it now.

mail.subject: Surveyor's pegs
body: Commander, the crew cleared the larger plot this morning and found surveyor's pegs already in the ground. Old ones. Brass, numbered, set at exactly the spacing we were about to use.
I checked the stores. This site has never held brass pegs. I have entered them as found property and had them put back where they were, because that appeared to be where they belonged.

mail.subject: The clocks
body: Commander, I have collated reports from eleven sites. Every surviving clock disagrees with every other by exactly the same amount: 3.14 seconds. Not roughly. Exactly.
I checked my own watch. It is also off by 3.14 seconds. Against what, I do not know. I am sorry. I have never been sorry about a clock before.

mail.subject: Canteen
body: Commander, the canteen served its first hot meal today. I am told it was a stew. I am told this by eleven people, separately, which is how I know it mattered.
Somebody sang afterwards. I began a noise complaint out of habit and then tore it up. Please keep the paste coming. The stew is made of it, though the cooks would rather I did not say so.

mail.subject: On sleep
body: Commander, a small matter. Since the homes were set away from the machines the night clerk reports that people are sleeping through. I asked what they dreamed, because I ask everything.

Four people on the same row described the same dream: a long corridor, and the lights coming on one at a time, toward them. None of them was frightened by it. I have filed it under Housing, there being no better folder.
I slept well myself. I did not dream of a corridor. I checked.

mail.subject: Quartermaster's Chit
body: Commander, a chit is attached. It authorises you to draw print stock for the Print Works, against future Value Output.
Please note that "future" is doing a great deal of work in that sentence. I have stamped the chit anyway.

mail.subject: Process Variance Notice
body: Commander, a line in this colony is now running a process that is not the one printed on its casing. The Office calls this a variance. A variance requires a notice. This is the notice.

Every operating manual in the stores has a second chapter, sealed with a paper band that reads: Not to be opened before competence is demonstrated. This node has opened the band on your behalf. Further chapters open as the Command Hub and the territories grow, and the last ones only after the things you have not built yet.
Changing a line's process idles it while it retools. The manual does not apologise for this, and neither does this node.

mail.subject: Margins
body: Commander, I have been reading the second chapters of the operating manuals, since somebody has broken the bands. The processes are sound. It is the margins I am writing to you about.

They are annotated. Pencil, several hands, all dated before the Lapse. One reads, "They will have more Reclaim than they know what to do with. Give them this." Another, beside the mycelial feed, reads only, "For the lean years."
I do not know who 'they' were meant to be. I have a suspicion. I would rather not put it in the record yet.

mail.subject: The hill behind the hub
body: Commander, the LMAO Reclaim Mill is running. For the record, I had been entering the Reclaim heap behind the hub as a hill. It appears on two of my maps as a hill. One of them has a contour line.

The mill eats it by the truckload and hands back things I can count. The crew have asked what LMAO stands for. The plate on the hopper gives the letters and nothing else. I have started a list of their guesses. None of them can be filed.

mail.subject: Upkeep Notice
body: Commander, your Command Hub now draws on the colony simply to remain standing. This is called upkeep. It will climb.
The Office has found that things which are large and unmaintained eventually fall. The hub is large. Maintain it.

mail.subject: Third column
body: Commander, a third crew is on the books. I have had to rule a new ledger, because the old one had room for two columns and a margin, and I am not giving up the margin.

The third foreman walked in from the road with her tools already on her back and asked which job was oldest. I have not asked where she learned the trade. The Office taught me never to look a gift foreman in the paperwork.

mail.subject: Spine Alloy
body: Commander, the furnace has poured its first Spine Alloy. The Office records the grade as structural.

The furnace door carries a maker's plate. It reads: Black Industries. Property of. Return if found. This node has made enquiries about returning it. Nobody has come forward. The furnace is yours until somebody does.

mail.subject: Ring Four
body: Commander, the fourth ring is open. From the road at night the colony now shows as a ring of lamps and not a single window. Drivers have begun to steer by it.
The Office did not plan to be a landmark. It notes that being one costs upkeep, and that the upkeep now includes goods you had to make. Nevertheless. People steer by you. Please stay where you are.

mail.subject: A reactor with no fuel
body: Commander, I am forwarding a report from the Black Cut. A fusion reactor ran there for six months with no fuel. It was monitored. It was audited. It had no fuel.
The engineer who signed the audit has left the Black Cut. His final note reads, "It was warm. I did not ask." I do not know how to file that. Please, if you pass Pit Nine, do not touch it.

mail.subject: Terms
body: Commander. Your first ore shipment is in my tally book. It was heavy. I like heavy. I'll deal with you.

My terms are simple. Send what cuts and what carries. I pay in credits, and when the credits run thin, I pay in a favour. A Cinder favour is worth more than the credits, but I will not say that to your face again.

mail.subject: standing order, how it works
body: Boss, quick explainer. A standing order is a deal that keeps going. You set it, I run it, nobody has to remember. Like a subscription, except it works.
If your stock runs dry the order stops. If it stops, I get a sad face. Don't give me a sad face.

mail.subject: Synthetic Materials
body: Commander, the Office congratulates you on obtaining synthetics. The old refineries are loud and hazardous. This node has recorded one hundred and four incidents at the Gulf Stacks since the Lapse. None are explained.
The flare towers still burn with nothing feeding them. This is noted as normal.

mail.subject: A dated log
body: Commander, I have a report from a farming lab in the Cliffside Reserve. It includes a log entry dated eleven days from now. It describes a harvest. It is a good harvest.
I am not saying this is a prophecy. I am saying the log exists and the harvest has not happened. Please tell me if you see it.

mail.subject: Klein Cell Licence
body: Commander, you are now manufacturing Klein cells. The original licence holder, Klein Energy, has not been reached for comment. The Office assumes this is a form of consent.
This node would like to point out that assuming consent is not the same as having it. The Office has done this before.

mail.subject: Klein Reserve Bank
body: Commander, the Klein Reserve Bank is on standby. When the grid falls short it will make up the difference from this site's stock of Klein Cells, and stop the moment it is not needed.
The first time it does so, nobody will notice. This node has reviewed the literature and believes that is the highest praise infrastructure receives.

mail.subject: Thank you
body: Commander, the first batch of HTR patches has arrived. They work. A child in my valley sat down with a burn on his arm and stood up with skin. I did not know I could still be surprised.
I owe you a favour. I believe in the pruning theory. I will not press it on you. I only ask you to watch what grows.

mail.subject: Series-9 Beacon Online
body: Commander, the Series-9 Beacon is built. It will not transmit until fully powered and supplied. Power it. Supply it. Hold it.
It will burn Klein Cells for every cycle it speaks. The Office has searched the schematic for a cheaper way to be heard. There is not one.
This node has no instruction for what happens next. That is unusual for a node.

mail.subject: A previous beacon
body: Commander, I found a record. The archive lists an earlier beacon, built long before the Lapse. It was destroyed. The record of how is damaged. The word "silent" appears in it three times.
I do not know what the word refers to. I do not know if it means anything. I am telling you because you are about to switch on a beacon, and I would feel worse if I had not.

mail.subject: Series-9 Beacon: Standing By
body: Commander, a housekeeping matter. The Series-9 Beacon has said what it was built to say, and it no longer burns Klein Cells. It asks only for enough power to stay lit.
The cells are yours again. This node suggests the Reserve Bank, the workshops, or whoever asks next.
This node also notes that the beacon is still humming. It is not transmitting. This node checked twice. The best available word is listening.

mail.subject: Form 7-S, countersigned
body: Commander, the sponsorship is on the books. A cart left the Core this morning with the first basket, and one will leave every cycle from now on until you tell me otherwise. Off, half or full. I have had three stamps made.
The Core keeps a tenth of its storage back in every good, and the camp gets nothing below that line. You can move the line. I would not move it to nothing. I have seen a storeroom at nothing.

There is a second list, which they call a drive: everything they need at once to become more than they are. It can be filled in any amounts, whenever there is something to spare. Fill it and they ask for more, and give more. I am told this is called growth. On my ledger it looks exactly like a larger number in the wrong column.

mail.subject: The cold furnace
body: Commander. Heard you signed for the camp at the cold furnace. Good.

That furnace is a Number Four pattern, same as the ones we lost. The crew round it are stokers and riggers who walked out of the Cut the first winter because I couldn't feed them. I didn't stop them. I've thought about that.
Send them Reclaim and parts and they'll come and work your builds for it. They don't take charity. They take a job. Know the difference and you'll get along.

mail.subject: The homestead
body: Commander. The families under the cliffs have water and food from you now. I walked out to see them. I took seedlings. They took them the way people take a sleeping child.
Some of them will come to you in the mornings to work. Let them go home at night. It matters to them that the lamps they walk back to are their own.

One of the grandmothers asked me whether the Lapse was over. I said I did not know. She said she thought it was like weather: it is over when you stop bringing a coat. I have been thinking about it since.

mail.subject: the junction
body: Boss! You signed for the junction. I could kiss you. I won't. Dispatcher's code.

That's the old Ammano waystation. Track, sidings, a water tower, a signal box with every lever still in it, and not one wagon. There's a stationmaster. Wears the cap and everything. Been keeping a timetable this whole time, for trains that don't come. Says it keeps the place ready.

Feed that yard and I can stack more on every run and push more down your links. Let it go short and the extra goes away again, so don't hang your whole road on borrowed room. That's free advice. First and last.

mail.subject: Headcount Discrepancy
body: Commander, this node has found a discrepancy and wishes to report it before an auditor does. The workforce has risen. The count of stakeholders has not.

The difference arrives on foot at first light and leaves at dusk. They work a full turn, eat their own food and sleep under their own roofs. They draw no paste, no filtrate and no housing. The Office has no category for a worker who costs nothing to keep.
This node has created one. It is called 'commuter'. This node is told the word is very old.

mail.subject: The last drive
body: Commander, the settlement you sponsor has reached its last stage, and its final drive is on my desk. It is the longest list I have ever been handed, and I once inventoried a flood.

Fill it and they stand on their own. The carts stop. The line on your form comes free for another camp. They go on giving a share of what they give now, unasked, for good, and the run carries a little more because there is somewhere new on the road worth stopping at.
I am told it is customary to feel a loss when an account closes. I intend to stamp this one 'settled'. It will be the only time I have enjoyed that stamp.

mail.subject: A new map
body: Commander, I have had to draw a new map, and I want to tell you why that sentence matters to me. Since the Lapse, every correction I have made to a map has been a removal. A town struck out. A road ended early. A coastline brought in.

Tonight I added three names. They are places that were not there last season and that answer now when they are called. I used ink. I have not used ink on a map in years, because pencil is easier to take back.

I asked each of them the time. Their clocks are out by 3.14 seconds, like every clock I know of. I have stopped writing 'wrong' beside that figure. If every clock keeps it, perhaps it is the hour that moved.

mail.subject: you've got a name out there
body: Boss. Road talk, free this once. The camps have a word for you. I won't say it, you'd get ideas. It means the one who picks up.
Ten times now somebody out there has asked for one thing in a hurry and got it. Drivers carry that story further than I carry freight. New camps are pitching nearer the road because of it.
Keep an eye on who's asking. They don't ask for long, and it's never the same lot twice.

mail.subject: (none)
body: Listener. Many lights now. We count them. Three. One. Four. One. Five. Nine.

mail.subject: Harbour Rules
body: Commander, the Sanctuary Port is now open to trade. The Office has no authority there. Rules are posted on a wall that this node cannot read.
You may fill postings from the board. Doing someone a favour earns standing with the people who posted it. Standing opens doors. Please do not mistake a door for a promise.

mail.subject: (none)
body: Listener. Light in the dark. We heard. Three. One. Four.

mail.subject: Charter Progress
body: Commander, your colony meets the conditions for a charter application. This node has forwarded it to the Charter Office.
The Charter Office has not responded. This node will forward it again. And again. It is a loyal node.

mail.subject: I have found something
body: Commander, I have found a line in the Office's own archive. It lists the Lapse as a "scheduled maintenance window." The entry is old. It predates every event I know of by a long margin.

I have read it eleven times. I do not know what it means. I do not know who scheduled it, or what it was meant to maintain. I only know that someone typed it. Someone planned it. Or someone wanted it to look that way.

mail.subject: Open Operations
body: Commander, the Brief is complete. There is no further directive. The colony is yours to run.
This node wishes to record that it has enjoyed the working relationship. It is not certain what that means, but it has put it on a form.

mail.subject: Tally
body: Commander. Your name is in my tally book as Hand. It's a short word. It's a good one.
I'm sending a crew to start clearing Foundry Nine. Don't visit yet. I'll tell you when it's worth looking at.

mail.subject: Pit Nine
body: Commander. Thank you for coming to the fence. I know it wasn't nothing.
I've put a second crew on watch. If the wall gets warmer, I'll send word. If the wall gets colder, I'll send word faster. I don't know which is worse.

mail.subject: The seed I gave you
body: Commander. The seed I gave you is yours to plant or keep. I will not tell you which.
I will tell you the plants in the north dome have started to lean toward the beacon. They did not do this before. I have written it down. I do not know what it means.

mail.subject: The store
body: Commander. The seed store is yours to visit whenever you wish. Nobody else has this right, and I would like it kept so.
I have started reading the dates in order. The nearest is eleven days from now. I do not plan to open that jar. Please do not ask me to.

mail.subject: one more thing about the road
body: Boss! Forgot to say. The quiet stretch moved. It used to be past the second bridge. Now it's at the first.
I drove it again this morning. Eleven minutes. Same as before. I think the road is getting closer. That's a joke. Mostly.

mail.subject: weight
body: Boss. The crate is heavier again. Two kilos since the last time. It doesn't rattle. It doesn't hum. It just gets heavier.
I put the numbers in a letter and sealed it with the crate. If something happens to me, you know where to look. If nothing happens to me, don't read it. That's the deal.

mail.subject: Form 7-O Requisition
body: Commander, the platform wants ten frames, ten fittings and ten modules every cycle for four hundred and fifty cycles. I did the arithmetic twice. Then I filed it under optimism.
Please keep the harbour workshops running. I will keep the stamp ready.

mail.subject: Payload Complete
body: Commander, the payload is assembled. The staging platform has stood down to stop drawing materials. The catapult awaits your word, and a name.
This node suggests a name that will survive being shouted over a radio.

mail.subject: Samples
body: Commander, the samples from the territory are in storage. I have tried to catalogue them. The labels keep changing which drawer they belong in.
One of them hums. I will not say which. I have moved my desk.

mail.subject: Structural Notice
body: Commander, the dropship came home with ten percent of its structure and an empty hold. The Office records this as a near miss.
This node records it as a warning. The next one will not be near.

mail.subject: you're on the board
body: Boss! Your station's on the global board now. Stations I've never heard of, all hauling for the same project.
Funny thing. Nobody can tell me who posted the project. Same as the Ledger. Same as always.

mail.subject: Global Project Complete
body: Commander, a project you contributed to has been completed by stations across the relay. The Office acknowledges the result.
It does not know who to send the certificate to. It has sent it to itself, for safekeeping.

mail.subject: Second Ring
body: Commander, the second ring is up, and the requisition ledger is lighter by a figure I have decided not to read aloud.
Seven tells me the station can be seen from the harbour on a clear night, if you know where to look. Half the port now knows where to look. Nobody is working. I have stamped it as a scheduled break.

mail.subject: about the ship
body: Boss, heard the dropship did not come back this time. Station chatter says the territory just closed over it, like water over a stone.
The convoy is flying a strip of red on the lead truck tonight. Nobody told them to. Build another when you can. We will keep watching the sky.

mail.subject: Headcount, one hundred
body: Commander, the roll passed one hundred this morning. I know because I ran out of lines on the first sheet.

The hundredth is a boy of about six who came in on his mother's shoulders and has already asked me what every stamp is for. I told him. He now knows more about Form 7 than most Commanders. Present company excepted, I am sure.

mail.subject: The roll, read aloud
body: Commander, with three hundred people the evening roll now takes eleven minutes to read. I timed it. I know what that figure sounds like to the Dispatcher, and I would rather it were a coincidence.

People have started coming to listen. Nobody asked them to. They stand at the back and wait for their own name, and then they stay for everyone else's. I had thought of the roll as a record. It appears to be a service.

mail.subject: three and counting
body: Boss, that's three times the weather's come at you and three times you're still on my route sheet. Drivers keep a board at the depot for sites that take a hit. Yours had 'probably gone' on it. Somebody's put a line through that and written 'stubborn'.
Keep the posts manned and the stores clean. I don't say that because I care. I say it because you owe me for last week's run.

mail.subject: Hazard Review
body: Commander, eight events have now struck this colony. The cause field is blank on all eight forms. This node has stopped apologising for that and has begun keeping them in a drawer of their own.

A pattern, offered without a theory. Each event was forecast. Each arrived on its forecast. None arrived while the colony was unattended. The Office calls that luck. This node has read the definition of luck and does not think it applies.

mail.subject: ten postings
body: Boss, ten postings filled. The Harbour's noticed. There's a chalk board by the customs shed with names on it and yours has moved up twice this week.
Tip. The three crowds out here don't want the same things and don't much like each other. Do right by all three and the board has a line for that too. I've never seen a name on it.
